# onetsolutions_hosting_database_user (Resource)

Manages a MySQL user of a web hosting.

## Password

The password is sent when the user is created and never read back: it is kept in the state
(marked sensitive) and an import cannot recover it. After an import, the configured password is
recorded as is, without changing the user's password.

~> **A new password recreates the user.** A database user's password cannot be changed in place:
a new `password` deletes the user and creates it again, which drops its privileges.
`onetsolutions_hosting_database_privileges` grants them again when it is replaced too, which
`replace_triggered_by` does, as in the example of that resource; otherwise the next plan finds them missing
and grants them again.

## Names

The web hosting prefixes every username with its own username and an underscore: `username =
"app"` on the web hosting of user `acme` creates `acme_app`, given in `full_username`. `username`
may be written with or without the prefix; changing one spelling for the other changes nothing.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "onetsolutions_web_hosting" "site" {
  domain = "example.com"
}

variable "database_password" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

resource "onetsolutions_hosting_database_user" "app" {
  hosting_id = data.onetsolutions_web_hosting.site.id
  username   = "app"
  password   = var.database_password
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `hosting_id` (String) The UUID of the web hosting. Changing it recreates the object in the other web hosting.
- `password` (String, Sensitive) The password of the user. A password cannot be changed in place: changing it recreates the user, which drops its privileges (see the page's notes). At least 8 characters with an uppercase letter, a lowercase letter, a digit and a special character. It is never read back: it is stored in the state, and an import cannot recover it.
- `username` (String) The name of the user: letters, digits and underscores, at most 16 characters. The web hosting's username and an underscore are prepended unless the name already starts with them (see `full_username`); both spellings are equivalent. Changing it recreates the user.

### Optional

- `organization_id` (String) The organization the object belongs to. Defaults to the provider's `organization_id` when the object is created; changing it explicitly recreates the object.
- `project_id` (String) The project the object belongs to. Defaults to the provider's `project_id` when the object is created; changing it explicitly recreates the object.

### Read-Only

- `full_username` (String) The username applications connect with, prefixed with the web hosting's username, such as `acme_app`.
- `id` (String) The full username, the same as `full_username`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = onetsolutions_hosting_database_user.app
  id = "3f2a9c1e-5b7d-4e8f-9a0b-1c2d3e4f5a6b/8b1d4e2f-6c3a-4f9e-8d7b-2a1c0e9f8d7c/5e7c2a1b-9d3f-4a6e-8b2c-1d0f9e8a7b6c/acme_app"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <organization_id>/<project_id>/<hosting_id>/<username>, or <hosting_id>/<username> when the provider sets
# organization_id and project_id. The password cannot be imported.
terraform import onetsolutions_hosting_database_user.app 3f2a9c1e-5b7d-4e8f-9a0b-1c2d3e4f5a6b/8b1d4e2f-6c3a-4f9e-8d7b-2a1c0e9f8d7c/5e7c2a1b-9d3f-4a6e-8b2c-1d0f9e8a7b6c/acme_app
```
